scenes.headline: How a mixture-of-experts layer runs a fraction of its weights
scenes.sub: The router, shared experts, load balancing and the all-to-all
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Inkwell! Mixture-of-experts models store far more weights than any one token uses. Here's how.

scenes.text: Replace the one feed-forward network with many experts, and let a small router send each token to only a few of them.
scenes.say: Swap the one feed-forward network for many experts, and route each token to just a few.

steps.say: The router, one small matrix, gives every expert a score for this token.

steps.note: Hunyuan-A13B: 64 routed experts, 8 run per token
steps.say: Keep the top eight of sixty-four. Only those eight experts run.
One shared expert runs on every token, so the routed ones can specialise.
Outputs are weighted by their gates, summed, and added to the residual stream.

scenes.title: Why total and active parameters differ
scenes.say: Every token skips the same share of the model.

parts.note: 64 experts, 8 chosen: 56 idle in each of 32 layers
parts.say: In each of thirty-two layers, fifty-six experts sit idle.
And each expert holds almost thirty-eight million weights.
So Hunyuan-A13B stores eighty billion weights but reads under thirteen billion per token.

scenes.title: Stored weights per active weight
scenes.note: total parameters divided by active parameters
scenes.say: Each generation widens the gap: under four stored weights per active one in Mixtral, almost twenty-seven in Kimi K3.

left.title: Auxiliary loss
items: Penalise uneven expert loads in the loss
Its gradient competes with language modelling
left.say: An extra loss evens the load, but its gradient fights the language model.

right.title: Routing bias
items: A per-expert bias, used only for choosing
Busy experts drift down, idle ones up
The gate stays the unbiased score
right.say: DeepSeek-V3 biases the scores for choosing only. Busy experts drift down, idle ones up.

scenes.title: Expert parallelism, one MoE layer
scenes.say: Spread across many GPUs, each MoE layer becomes a round trip.

items.text: Route on the token's own GPU
items.say: Route each token where it lives.
An all-to-all ships it to its experts' GPUs.
Each GPU runs its own experts.
A second all-to-all brings the outputs home.

scenes.text: A router lets parameters grow while compute per token stays flat; the cost moves into memory, balance and communication.
scenes.say: Experts add knowledge, not compute per token. The bill moves to memory, balance and the network.

recap: Router: score every expert, run the top k
Total grows with experts, active with k
Balance with a bias, ship by all-to-all
scenes.say: Score, and keep the top few. Balance the load. Ship tokens to their experts.
